targetCompanyImage.name: Brightspeed
targetCompanyImage.description: Brightspeed owns and operates wireline telecommunications and fiber broadband infrastructure in the United States. Its customers include residential broadband subscribers, businesses, and wholesale communications counterparties, and the business is investing capital into a largely asset-heavy fiber upgrade program across a legacy local-exchange footprint. Public disclosures describe operations across 20 states and a long-term plan to expand fiber coverage materially within that footprint. The company was formed in connection with Apollo-managed funds' acquisition of Lumen's incumbent local exchange carrier business and launched the Brightspeed brand in 2021 ahead of the transaction close. Mubadala announced a $500 million minority investment in Brightspeed in May 2023. The reviewed public materials do not disclose Mubadala's ownership percentage or the detailed current ownership split among Apollo-managed vehicles.

seedEntry.name: Brightspeed
seedEntry.ownershipVehicle: Apollo-managed funds (including AIOF II Connect Holdings, L.P.)
seedEntry.description: Brightspeed owns and operates wireline telecommunications and fiber broadband infrastructure across 20 U.S. states from Charlotte, North Carolina. Apollo-managed funds completed the acquisition of Lumen's incumbent local exchange carrier operations in October 2022. The FCC's 2022 approval order for the subsequently consummated acquisition shows that the Apollo ownership group included AIOF II Connect Holdings, L.P., a vehicle of Apollo Infrastructure Opportunities Fund II, with a direct interest of less than 5% alongside larger Apollo private-equity and co-invest vehicles; the 2% equity and 3% voting values appeared only in the December 2023 proposed post-Mubadala structure. Mubadala signed a $500 million minority investment through CEPSA Holding LLC in May 2023, and the FCC approved the proposed foreign-ownership structure in December 2023; no public legal-closing announcement or date was found, so Mubadala remains a signed pending incoming investor in this census. Brightspeed completed a debt recapitalization in August 2024 that issued warrants and preferred stock, and the current exact ownership percentages are not publicly disclosed. No Apollo or Mubadala exit was found through August 8, 2026.

milestones.event: Apollo-managed private-equity funds announced an agreement to acquire Lumen's incumbent local exchange carrier business in 20 U.S. states.
Brightspeed unveiled its brand for the pending Apollo acquisition of Lumen's ILEC operations.
Apollo-managed funds completed the acquisition from Lumen and Brightspeed began operating the business.
Mubadala and Brightspeed announced a signed $500 million minority investment subject to regulatory approvals and other closing conditions; no public legal-closing date was found.

The FCC approved Brightspeed's proposed post-Mubadala foreign-ownership structure, which showed pro forma interests of 2% equity for AIOF II and approximately 28% proposed equity for Mubadala through CEPSA Holding LLC.

Brightspeed completed a debt recapitalization that secured approximately $3.7 billion of new financing, eliminated approximately $1.1 billion of debt and issued warrants and preferred stock to participating lenders.
